subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw preserve automatic bare-text visible replies as the default while suppressing proven internal/commentary/reasoning paths, or move channel/source delivery toward explicit message-tool-only semantics by default?
rationale: The source and docs show automatic visible replies are a current public behavior, but the issue discussion shows that behavior can leak sensitive internal text to real messaging channels; automation cannot safely choose the compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Staged guarded delivery
options.body: Keep existing automatic final-reply compatibility for now, but suppress phase-tagged commentary, structured reasoning, obvious non-final tool-turn buffers, and cron reasoning payloads with tests and a later default-policy follow-up.

options.title: Explicit-send default
options.body: Make source/channel replies visible only through message(action=send) by default and provide a migration or opt-out for deployments that rely on bare final text.

options.title: Opt-in escape hatches only
options.body: Land only opt-in controls such as final-tag enforcement or message-tool-only config, leaving the current automatic default unchanged for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Staged guarded delivery
recommendation.body: Keep existing automatic final-reply compatibility for now, but suppress phase-tagged commentary, structured reasoning, obvious non-final tool-turn buffers, and cron reasoning payloads with tests and a later default-policy follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is a cross-channel safety and compatibility policy decision, and this handle has recent member triage context on adjacent reasoning-leak policy plus related channel/provider history.
